(x-4)+(f(x)-39)(x-4)=0
\]

\[
(x-4)\bigl(f(x)-38\bigr)=0.
\]

---

### Case 1: \(x=4\)

Then \(f(4)=-2\), so \(P=(4,-2)\).  
Distance to \(C\):

\[
r=|39-(-2)|=41.
\]

---

### Case 2: \(f(x)=38\)

Solve

\[
\frac{(x-4)^2}{2}-2=38
\implies (x-4)^2=80.
\]

So \(x-4=\pm 4\sqrt5\).  
At such a point, \(y=38\), hence the vertical separation from \(C\) is \(38-39=-1\).

Thus

\[
r=\sqrt{(x-4)^2+(-1)^2}
=\sqrt{80+1}=\sqrt{81}=9.
\]

Both choices of \(x\) give the same radius \(r=9\).

---

No other possibilities exist (the normal is undefined only when \(x=4\), already handled).

The real radii for which a tangency occurs are

\[
r=9 \quad\text{and}\quad r=41.
\]

Their sum is

\[
9+41=50.
\]

\[
\boxed{50}
\]
